name: TimescaleDB 2.32 on PostgreSQL 18
description: Time-series Postgres with TimescaleDB, PgBouncer and daily backups.

upstream.timescaledb: timescale/timescaledb:2.32.1-pg18 (TimescaleDB 2.32.1 on PostgreSQL 18, Alpine; also pgvector; digest sha256:70e6526ad8e31e3f4833f2c5863b50b92d7a6bee4d432ad1f660e2c6dd956d94, built 2026-11-19)

PGDATA.description: Data directory, a subfolder of the volume (the volume root holds lost+found and the TLS certificate).

POSTGRES_PASSWORD.description: Superuser password, generated at deploy (32 letters, URL-safe). Changing it later needs ALTER USER as well.

POSTGRES_DB.description: Database created on first boot, with the timescaledb and pg_stat_statements extensions.

PGHOST.description: Private hostname (timescaledb.railway.internal), for Railway's Data tab and libpq clients.

PGPORT.description: PostgreSQL port on the private network.

DATABASE_URL.description: Direct connection over the private network: migrations, bulk ingest (COPY, timescaledb-parallel-copy), LISTEN/NOTIFY.

DATABASE_PUBLIC_URL.description: Connection from outside Railway through the TCP proxy, TLS required (self-signed certificate; egress is billed).

DATABASE_POOL_URL.description: Pooled connection through PgBouncer (transaction mode, private network). Use it for application queries.

TIMESCALEDB_LICENSE.description: timescale = all community features (compression, continuous aggregates, retention jobs) under the Timescale License; apache = Apache-2.0 features only.

TIMESCALEDB_TELEMETRY.description: off or basic: TimescaleDB's anonymous usage telemetry.

TS_TUNING.description: auto = size memory, WAL and parallel workers from the service limits at every boot; off = PostgreSQL defaults.

TS_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB.description: RAM the tuning plans for. auto = the service limit capped at 8192 MB; set a number after raising memory.

TS_CPU_LIMIT.description: CPUs the tuning plans for. auto = the service CPU quota capped at 8.

TS_MAX_CONNECTIONS.description: max_connections. Apps should connect through PgBouncer (DATABASE_POOL_URL).

TS_MAX_BACKGROUND_WORKERS.description: timescaledb.max_background_workers: compression, retention and continuous-aggregate jobs running at once.

SSL_CERT_DAYS.description: Validity of the self-signed TLS certificate; renewed at a boot within 30 days of expiry.

RAILWAY_SHM_SIZE_BYTES.description: Size of /dev/shm (1 GiB; Railway's default is 64 MB). Parallel queries need shared memory; only memory in use is billed.

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Time PostgreSQL gets to shut down cleanly on redeploy.

PORT.description: Port of the healthcheck helper (private only; PostgreSQL listens on 5432).

DB_HOST.description: TimescaleDB private hostname that PgBouncer forwards to.

DB_USER.description: TimescaleDB superuser; written to PgBouncer's userlist and used as auth_user, so other roles can log in through the pool too.

DB_PASSWORD.description: Password of that user (kept in sync by reference).

AUTH_TYPE.description: Client authentication; matches PostgreSQL's SCRAM password encryption.

LISTEN_ADDR.description: Listen on IPv4 and IPv6 (Railway's private DNS returns both; some clients try IPv6 first).

LISTEN_PORT.description: PgBouncer port on the private network.

POOL_MODE.description: transaction = a server connection per transaction (best multiplexing). Use session for apps that need session state.

DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE.description: Server connections per database/user pair; keep the total under TimescaleDB max_connections (TS_MAX_CONNECTIONS, 100 by default).

MAX_PREPARED_STATEMENTS.description: Protocol-level prepared statements tracked per connection, so drivers that prepare statements work in transaction mode. 0 disables.

ADMIN_USERS.description: Users allowed to run SHOW POOLS / SHOW STATS on the pgbouncer admin database.

DATABASE_POOL_URL.description: Pooled connection string for your apps (also exposed on the TimescaleDB service). No TLS: it stays on the private network.

PGUSER.description: Superuser, needed to dump roles and every database.

PGDATABASE.description: Database used to list the others.

PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT.description: Seconds before a connection attempt gives up (the job retries while TimescaleDB starts).

PGAPPNAME.description: application_name shown in pg_stat_activity while a backup runs.

BACKUP_S3_BUCKET.description: Railway Bucket that stores the backups.

BACKUP_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE.description: Keep false: Railway Buckets use virtual-hosted-style URLs. true only for buckets whose Credentials tab says path-style.

BACKUP_PREFIX.description: Folder in the bucket; each run writes {prefix}/{UTC timestamp}/.

BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS.description: Delete complete runs older than this many days.

BACKUP_KEEP_MIN.description: Always keep at least this many complete runs, whatever their age.

BACKUP_COMPRESSION.description: pg_dump --compress value for the custom-format dumps (zstd:3, gzip:6, lz4, none).

BACKUP_DATABASES.description: Databases to dump, comma-separated. Empty = every database that accepts connections.

BACKUP_WAIT_SECONDS.description: How long a run waits for TimescaleDB to accept connections before failing.

RESTORE_RUN.description: Restore only (start command /usr/local/bin/timescaledb-backup restore): run folder to restore, or latest.

RESTORE_DATABASE.description: Restore only: database to restore from that run. Empty = PGDATABASE.

RESTORE_TARGET.description: Restore only: NEW database to restore into. Empty = {database}_restored; an existing database is never overwritten.
